_doc: Famous readers' own published words about a book. Public domain in the US. Every `text` must be a verbatim substring of the Gutenberg file named by `gutenberg` (scripts/build_index.py fails the build otherwise). Add a line by adding an entry; never type a quote from memory.

35698.work: Letters of John Keats to His Family and Friends

76513.work: Hawthorne and His Mosses (1850), in Billy Budd and Other Prose Pieces

lines.title: King Lear
lines.author: William Shakespeare
lines.text: I sat down yesterday to read King Lear once again: the thing appeared to demand the prologue of a sonnet, I wrote it, and began to read

lines.title: Moby-Dick
lines.author: Herman Melville
lines.text: But it is a great book, a very great book, the greatest book of the sea ever written. It moves awe in the soul.

lines.title: The Scarlet Letter
lines.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
lines.text: The Scarlet Letter isn't a pleasant, pretty romance. It is a sort of parable, an earthly story with a hellish meaning.

lines.title: Leaves of Grass
lines.author: Walt Whitman
lines.text: Whitman, the great poet, has meant so much to me. Whitman, the one man breaking a way ahead. Whitman, the one pioneer.

lines.title: Mosses from an Old Manse
lines.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
lines.text: But already I feel that this Hawthorne has dropped germinous seeds into my soul.

lines.title: Middlemarch
lines.author: George Eliot
lines.text: the magnificent book which with all its imperfections is one of the few English novels written for grown-up people.

lines.title: Wuthering Heights
lines.author: Emily Brontë
lines.text: Wuthering Heights is a more difficult book to understand than Jane Eyre, because Emily was a greater poet than Charlotte.

lines.title: Jane Eyre
lines.author: Charlotte Brontë
lines.text: So we open Jane Eyre; and in two pages every doubt is swept clean from our minds.

lines.title: Robinson Crusoe
lines.author: Daniel Defoe
lines.text: The book resembles one of the anonymous productions of the race itself rather than the effort of a single mind

lines.title: Pride and Prejudice
lines.author: Jane Austen
lines.text: the most perfect artist among women, the writer whose books are immortal
